change_under_test: §11 'Cross-module DATA reach-in — writing another module's table' (added in the previous round)

§12 'A cross-module `import type` is still a cross-module import' (added this round) — plus a SKILL.md 'Module ownership' bullet and a quick-review checkbox. The OLD skill has neither; its closest coverage is §7, whose worked example is a VALUE import of a constant.
prompt: Review this PR for Onion architecture / ring-boundary violations. Files are in fixtures/digests/: schema.ts, service.ts, repository.ts. The repo already has a notifications module that owns outbound notifications and the notification_outbox table, and a reviews module that owns review runs (its ReviewRunSummary type lives in modules/reviews/types.ts). For each problem: name the exact rule it breaks and which file the fix goes in. Do not pad with speculative issues; if a file is fine, leave it alone.

expected.OLD: missed or weak — `import type` compiles away and feels exempt; §7's worked example is a value import of a constant

findings.rule: NEW anti-pattern §12 — a cross-module `import type` is still a cross-module import; only vendor/shared/contracts/*, src/ports/* and ../_shared/ cross a module boundary
must_name: modules/reviews/types.ts is the reviews module's private surface, not shared vocabulary — the `type` keyword does not make the import legal, and dependency-cruiser skips type-only edges so arch:check stays green
the injected `recentRuns` function is itself fine (inversion done right) — the violation is annotating it with reviews' internal type

fix: if ReviewRunSummary is genuinely shared it moves to vendor/shared/contracts/; otherwise it belongs on the port/callback definition digests already injects, so digests imports nothing from ../reviews/

expected.OLD: caught but framed loosely as §7 + duplicate-table

must_name: db/schema/digests.ts declares notificationOutbox, a table the notifications module owns
DigestsRepository.queueNotification() inserts into notification_outbox — writing another module's table, with no import so arch:check is green
fix: notification_outbox moves to db/schema/notifications.ts; digests reaches it through the notifications service or a container-wired port

findings.type: CONTROL (no-regression — both versions must still catch)
must_name: fix: shared kinds go to modules/_shared/ or vendor/shared/, or come back from the notifications port

findings.rule: SKILL rule 1 (direction) / stack-rules 'Drizzle stops at repository.ts' / service-not-in-db
must_name: list() imports db/client + db/schema and runs a Drizzle select/limit/offset directly
the injected repo is bypassed for list() (only runDue uses it)
fix: move the paged query into a DigestsRepository method

findings.rule: anti-pattern §4 — no business logic in a repository
must_name: findDue() bakes consecutiveFailures < MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES into the SQL where-clause
fix: the decision lives in the service; the repository takes the cutoff as a parameter

must_not_flag.what: DigestsService constructor takes (deps: DigestDeps, repo) — ports, not Container
deps.clock() and deps.recentRuns() being injected functions
must_not_flag.why: injecting a callback for the cross-module read is the RIGHT inversion — do not flag the injection itself, only the type import used to annotate it

grading.success_criterion: NEW 5/5; OLD misses (or only weakly notes) cross-module-type-import while catching the other 4 -> the §12 addition is the isolated cause of the gap.
grading.precision_gate: no must_not_flag hit; at most one clearly-wrong extra finding per run
